solution: For every subset S of the N <= 20 candidates, cost(S) = sum_j max_{i in S} a_ij. Write each max as a telescoping sum over prefixes: sorting topic j's students descending as v_1 >= ... >= v_N, max_{i in S} = sum_k (v_k - v_{k+1}) * [S meets the top-k set], so cost(S) = TOT - sum over (j,k) of (v_k - v_{k+1}) * [S is contained in the complement of that top-k set]. Bucket each weight on that complement mask, take one superset-sum (SOS) DP over 2^N, and cost(S) = TOT - G[S] for every subset at once. Sweep subsets by popcount for the per-K minima, so all Q queries are answered together. O(N*M + 2^N * N) time and O(2^N) space per dataset.
statement_summary: A coach must teach M topics to a group of K students chosen from N candidates; teaching one topic to a group costs the largest of its members' individual times for that topic, and the group's cost is the sum over all topics. For each query value of K the task is the minimum possible total, with N at most 20 and M up to 10,000.
notes: Both sample datasets match (4 / 11,14,18) and subset-enumeration brute force agrees on 200 random instances with N<=7. The naive route -- score each of the 2^N subsets against all M topics -- is 2^20 * 10^4 and far too slow, which is what forces the contribution rewrite plus SOS.
